messages.author: f4ac9004a21f0fed
messages.subject: Troubleshooting in Rattle Install
parts:
Dear All

I used Ubuntu packages for most of the install (like ATK, Pango, libglade,GTK,xml) , installed Rattle (and pmml) from source and then got an error while starting Rattle

> library(rattle)
Rattle: Graphical interface for data mining using R.
Version 2.6.0 Copyright (c) 2006-2010 Togaware Pty Ltd.
Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> rattle()
Error in rattle() : attempt to apply non-function
In addition: Warning message:
In method(obj, ...) : Invalid object type `GtkListStore'
Rattle timestamp (for the error above): 2010-12-18 15:05:58
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

so now i followed the instructions here

> rattle.info()
Rattle: version 2.6.0
R: version 2.11.1 (2010-05-31) (Revision 52157)

Sysname: Linux
Release: 2.6.35-23-generic
Version: #41-Ubuntu SMP Wed Nov 24 10:18:49 UTC 2010
Nodename: k1-M725R
Machine: i686
Login: k
User: k

Installed Dependencies
RGtk2: version 2.12.18 upgrade available 2.20.3
pmml: version 1.2.26
colorspace: version 1.0-1
cairoDevice: version 2.14
e1071: version 1.5-24
ellipse: version 0.3-5
foreign: version 0.8-41
Hmisc: version 3.8-3
kernlab: version 0.9-12
Matrix: version 0.999375-46
mice: version 2.4
network: version 1.5-1
nnet: version 7.3-1
party: version 0.9-99991
randomForest: version 4.5-36 upgrade available 4.6-1
rggobi: version 2.1.16
survival: version 2.36-2
XML: version 3.2-0
bitops: version 1.0-4.1

Upgrade the packages with:

  > install.packages(c("RGtk2", "randomForest"))



I then installed these packages and wow, it works. Just thought of sharing this since this was the easiest rattle install i have seen - thanks for the updated documentation

regards

ajay

Websites-
http://decisionstats.com






On Wed, Dec 1, 2010 at 6:31 AM, Leeman <in...@frenergy.com.au> wrote:
I am running Windows XP SP3. I have spent the last 4 days trying to
get a proper installation of this program without success.

I follow the instructions as per http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/Internet_Connected.html


> library(rattle)
Rattle: Graphical interface for data mining using R.
Version 2.5.47 Copyright (c) 2006-2010 Togaware Pty Ltd.
Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> rattle()
Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) :
 unable to load shared object 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-212~1.0/library/RGtk2/
libs/i386/RGtk2.dll':
 LoadLibrary failure:  The specified procedure could not be found.


Failed to load RGtk2 dynamic library, attempting to install it.
trying URL 'http://downloads.sourceforge.net/gtk-win/gtk2-
runtime-2.22.0-2010-10-21-ash.exe?download'
Content type 'application/x-msdos-program' length 7820679 bytes (7.5
Mb)
opened URL
downloaded 7.5 Mb

Learn more about GTK+ at http://www.gtk.org
If the package still does not load, please ensure that GTK+ is
installed and that it is on your PATH environment variable
IN ANY CASE, RESTART R BEFORE TRYING TO LOAD THE PACKAGE AGAIN
Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType
>


I havve installed, completly uninstalled, removed *.rdata file (which
was crashing the system onload)

I have 1 day before my university course ends lectures on this subject
and i have not completed a single lab exercise.

I am at a loss of what to do.


I restart, i uninstall GTK+, i reinstall, then crashes...

AppName: rgui.exe        AppVer: 2.120.53317.0   ModName: msvcrt.dll
ModVer: 7.0.2600.5512    Offset: 00037fd4


When I restart R, and type in

library(rattle)

then

Rattle()

I get a popup, "the procedure entry point deflateSetHeader could not
be located in the dynamic link library zlib1.dll

continually doing this, I RESTART as instructed etc etc.

messages.author: f4ac9004a21f0fed
messages.subject: Re: Troubleshooting in Rattle Install
parts:
Hi Tony

For Ubuntu the wajig mode is kind of irrelevant- you may want to tell users to directly install packages from Ubuntu Software centre, and then install Rattle from source

I think making the instructions more granular as Step 1 Step 2 .. may help simplify things even more

Also you may want to advise using VM Player and Ubuntu for people with pure Windows given the trouble GTK+ gets. My view is that GTK is the culprit when it comes to the installation difficulties

Regards

Ajay

Websites-
http://decisionstats.com
